FELLMOOR SUPERIOR COURT OF JUSTICE

BETWEEN: Corwin Ashby, Plaintiff – and – Brindle Hardware Inc., Defendant

BEFORE: Justice R. Okonkwo-Hale

HEARD: May 12–14, 2095

REASONS FOR JUDGMENT

[1]The plaintiff, Corwin Ashby, claims damages for injuries suffered when he slipped on an icy walkway outside the defendant's hardware store in Fellmoor on January 9, 2094.
[2]The defendant, Brindle Hardware Inc., denies liability. It says the walkway was salted twice that morning, and that the plaintiff was not paying attention because he was using his telephone.
[3]The issues are: (a) whether the defendant breached the standard of care under the Occupiers' Liability Act; (b) whether the plaintiff was contributorily negligent; and (c) the quantum of damages.
  1. Was the walkway reasonably maintained given the weather that morning?
  2. Did the plaintiff's own inattention contribute to the fall?

Analysis

[4]I accept the evidence of the store manager that salt was applied at 7:30 a.m. However, freezing rain began at about 9:15 a.m., and no further salt was applied before the plaintiff fell at 11:05 a.m.
[5]An occupier must take such care as in all the circumstances is reasonable to see that persons entering the premises are reasonably safe.1 In light of the changing weather, a reasonable occupier would have inspected and re-salted the walkway before late morning.
[6]I find the defendant liable. I reduce the plaintiff's recovery by twenty per cent for contributory negligence, given his own evidence that he was reading a message as he walked.
Damages summary
HeadAmount
General damages$45,000
Special damages$6,200
[7] General damages are assessed at $45,000 and special damages at $6,200, for a total of $51,200 before the reduction.
[8] After the twenty per cent reduction, judgment will issue for the plaintiff in the amount of $40,960, with prejudgment interest under the Courts of Justice Act.
[9] If the parties cannot agree on costs, they may make brief written submissions within thirty days.

Justice R. Okonkwo-Hale

Released: June 2, 2095

1 Occupiers' Liability Act, R.S.F. 2080, c. O.2, s. 3(1).
